description: Test your knowledge of the Transformer architecture, attention mechanisms, and how LLMs predict the next word.

questions.question: What does GPT stand for?
options: General Purpose Technology
Generative Pre-trained Transformer
Google's Primary Tool
questions.explanation: GPT = Generative (creates text) + Pre-trained (already learned from data) + Transformer (the architecture). All modern LLMs use this pattern — OpenAI just named their assistant ChatGPT.

questions.question: What problem did Transformers solve that RNNs/LSTMs couldn't?
options: Making AI models cheaper to run
Understanding long-range relationships in text by processing entire sequences at once
Translating between programming languages
questions.explanation: RNNs processed text word-by-word and lost context over long distances. Transformers (2017) read entire sequences at once using attention — capturing relationships like 'it' referring to 'cat' across the sentence.

questions.question: In 'The cat sat on the mat because it was tired', what does self-attention help with?
options: Counting the number of words in the sentence
Figuring out that 'it' refers to 'cat', not 'mat'
Translating the sentence to another language
questions.explanation: Self-attention lets each token look at all other tokens in the sentence. The model learns 'it' is more related to 'cat' than 'mat' — solving ambiguous pronoun references.

questions.question: What is causal (masked) self-attention?
options: Attention that only looks at future words
Attention that blocks the model from seeing future tokens — only past and present
Attention that ignores all previous words
questions.explanation: Causal attention ensures information flows one direction: past → present. When predicting the next word, the model can only see tokens before the current position, never future ones.

questions.question: What is the role of a Feed-Forward Network (FFN) in a Transformer layer?
options: It lets tokens communicate with each other
It processes each token independently after attention — deepening its representation
It converts text to token IDs
questions.explanation: Attention = tokens talk to each other (context). FFN = each token thinks independently about what it learned. 'Bank' finds river meaning during attention; FFN deepens that understanding per token.

questions.question: What do residual (skip) connections do in a Transformer?
options: Skip the entire Transformer and use RNN instead
Add the original input back to the layer's output — preserving info while adding updates
Remove unnecessary tokens from the input
questions.explanation: Instead of replacing old info, residual connections do: output = original input + layer update. This lets each layer refine understanding without losing what previous layers learned.

questions.question: How does the model pick the final next word?
options: It randomly selects from the vocabulary
Linear layer reshapes output → Softmax converts to probabilities → highest probability wins
It always picks the first word in the vocabulary
questions.explanation: After all Transformer layers, a Linear layer reshapes the output and Softmax converts scores into percentages (summing to 100%). The word with the highest probability becomes the predicted next token.
